metaData.originalTitle: An entire Herculaneum scroll has been read for the first time
metaData.title: An entire Herculaneum scroll has been read for the first time
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: A team has virtually unwrapped and read an entire Herculaneum scroll (PHerc. 1667) for the first time using X-ray imaging and machine learning, revealing a Stoic philosophical text.
metaData.summary: This article announces a historic breakthrough: the complete virtual unwrapping and reading of PHerc. 1667, a carbonized scroll from Herculaneum sealed since 79 AD. The scroll was scanned with high-resolution phase-contrast X-ray microtomography at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility, then digitally flattened and read using machine learning to detect faint ink. The recovered text is a Stoic philosophical treatise, possibly by Chrysippus or his school. The same method also confirmed the reading of another scroll (PHerc. Paris 4) with higher-resolution imaging and identified the title and author of PHerc. 139 (Philodemus, On Gods, Book 8). All data, code, and transcriptions are openly released, and the work was achieved via the open Vesuvius Challenge community.

mainPoints.point: First complete virtual unwrapping and reading of a sealed Herculaneum scroll.
mainPoints.explanation: PHerc. 1667 was virtually unrolled and its text read from end to end for the first time, without physical opening.

mainPoints.point: Machine learning on high-resolution X-ray scans reveals carbon-based ink.
mainPoints.explanation: ML models trained on synchrotron CT data detect ink indistinguishable from carbonized papyrus, enabling reading.

mainPoints.point: The recovered text is a Stoic philosophical treatise with ethical themes.
mainPoints.explanation: The text discusses human nature, impulse, and moral progress, naming Aristocreon (nephew of Chrysippus), dating to 2nd century BC.

mainPoints.point: Independent confirmation via higher-resolution imaging of Scroll 1.
mainPoints.explanation: PHerc. Paris 4 was re-scanned at higher resolution, making ink directly visible in 3D and matching the 2023 Grand Prize reading one-to-one.

mainPoints.point: All research outputs are open, enabling scaling to the remaining library.
mainPoints.explanation: Data, code, and transcriptions are released under Creative Commons and on GitHub, allowing anyone to verify and build upon the work.

keyQuotes: The thoughts of the ancient world, sealed in darkness for two millennia, are coming back into the light --- a whole scroll at a time.
For almost 2,000 years, the carbonized library of Herculaneum has kept a cruel bargain: its scrolls survived the eruption of Mount Vesuvius, but only by becoming too fragile to open.
...we will inquire into something, but we will not grasp it, if in some way we depart from ourselves and from our own nature...

relatedArticles.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI engineers detail a five-month experiment building a production software product with zero manually-written code, using Codex agents to achieve 10x velocity and redefining the engineer's role as system designer and feedback loop architect.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.0 with Thinking-Level Intelligence
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Images 2.0, a state-of-the-art image model featuring sharper editing, richer layouts, and reasoning capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: Software Architecture Guide
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This page from Martin Fowler presents his perspective on software architecture, defining it as the important stuff in system design, and serves as a curated guide to his site's extensive resources on application and enterprise architecture.

relatedArticles.title: Dario Amodei — Policy on the AI Exponential
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Dario Amodei argues that AI is advancing exponentially, creating a dangerous mismatch with slow-moving policy, and proposes concrete actions across regulation, economics, science, civil liberties, and geopolitics to meet the moment.

relatedArticles.title: Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6: Enhanced Embodied Reasoning
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Google DeepMind introduces Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6, a significant upgrade to its embodied reasoning model that enhances spatial understanding, multi-view reasoning, and introduces new capabilities like instrument reading for real-world robotics applications.

relatedArticles.title: Continual learning for AI agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article defines a three-layer framework—Model, Harness, and Context—for implementing continual learning in AI agents, moving beyond simple weight updates to include code optimization and persistent memory.

relatedArticles.title: Xiaomi MiMo， Explore and Love
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Xiaomi MiMo and TileRT achieve 1000+ tokens/s inference on a 1-trillion-parameter model using commodity GPUs through extreme model-system codesign, including FP4 quantization and DFlash speculative decoding.

relatedArticles.title: Inside FAISS: Billion-Scale Similarity Search
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep, visual, and intuitive explanation of FAISS, covering the core ideas of IVF, Product Quantization, their combination in IVFPQ, and GPU acceleration, to enable billion-scale similarity search.

relatedArticles.title: Stop Treating AI Memory Like a Search Problem
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article critiques the conventional 'store-and-retrieve' approach to AI memory, proposing a lifecycle-based system with decay, contradiction detection, confidence scoring, compression, and expiry to manage memory like a human brain rather than a static archive.

relatedArticles.title: Falcon Perception
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Falcon Perception is a 0.6B early-fusion Transformer that unifies vision and language in a single backbone for open-vocabulary grounding and segmentation, outperforming SAM 3 on complex compositional prompts.
